evidence: Parent (3e73) states: '[operator-attested] every pin or rewrite added under this epic is MUTATION-CHECKED — the mutation applied and the resulting verdict recorded as a comment on the owning child ticket. A pin nobody has seen fail is not evidence. Copied terminal output showing the mutated code and the resulting FAIL, pasted as a child-ticket comment, satisfies this criterion; it is attested rather than CI-checkable because a mutation is applied and reverted in a working tree and therefore leaves no repo artifact to inspect'

Sibling cedc (cedc-58d1-f6d1-428e) explicitly carries the full attestation requirement in its ACs: 'every new pin is mutation-checked, with the mutation and the resulting verdict recorded BOTH as a comment on this ticket (cedc-58d1-f6d1-428e) in the format `MUTATED: <symbol> <old_value> -> <wrong_value>; FAILED: <test_id>`, AND as a module-level comment block in the test file so the evidence is a committed, diff-reviewable repo artifact'

Leaf (79d5) mutation-checking ACs say only: 'mutation-checked for the injection itself: REMOVING the explicit injection ... turns the DC cells RED' and 'mutation-checked: raising the limit above the real ceiling, or removing the fit, turns a convergence test red' — no mention of recording verdicts as a ticket comment or module-level block
findings.finding: The leaf's mutation-checking ACs omit the operator-attestation recording requirement that the parent epic mandates for every pin or rewrite: the parent requires the mutation verdict to be 'recorded as a comment on the owning child ticket' (in the format `MUTATED: <symbol> <old_value> -> <wrong_value>; FAILED: <test_id>`) AND 'as a module-level comment block in the test file so the evidence lands in the diff.' The leaf's ACs say only that removing the injection turns cells RED — they never require either attestation record. This omission means an implementer who mutation-checks but does not produce either record fully satisfies the leaf's ACs while violating the parent's.
findings.location: Leaf AC section — mutation-checked bullets; Parent epic AC: '[operator-attested] every pin or rewrite added under this epic is MUTATION-CHECKED'
scenarios: An implementer mutation-checks, sees RED, reverts — but records nothing. The leaf ACs are fully satisfied; the parent's operator-attestation requirement is not.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the concrete discriminating assertion for the DESCRIPTION test: e.g. 'feed a 33 000-character plain-text input, assert `len(truncated_body) <= 32767` AND that the truncated body is plain text (no ADF JSON wrapper), since Cloud's path would either reject or serialize-inflate the same input past 32000 ADF chars'.
evidence: Plan states: 'DC fits plain characters at WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT (32767), while Cloud fits ADF-SERIALIZED size at _ADF_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT (32000). Those genuinely differ, so a length/ADF-shape assertion here would FAIL if the fallback supplied Cloud\'s mapper'
No specific assertion is stated — e.g. 'assert len(result) <= 32767 and not result.startswith(\'{\"type\"')' or 'assert len(plain_text_input) > 32000 and len(truncated) <= 32767'

Absence: the AC says the assertion 'would FAIL' under Cloud's mapper, but does not say WHAT the assertion IS, leaving the executor to invent a discriminating check that might or might not actually fail under Cloud's ADF path
findings.finding: The VALUE-BASED discriminator for the DESCRIPTION convergence test is specified as a goal ('a length/ADF-shape assertion here would FAIL if the fallback supplied Cloud's mapper') but the concrete assertion to write is never stated. The executor must invent it without guidance, making the AC unevaluable as written.
findings.location: Acceptance criteria — 'the DESCRIPTION test proves it exercised DC's fit by a VALUE-BASED discriminator'
scenarios: An executor writes a plain `assert plan == []` for pass 2, which passes under both backends since both truncate and converge, and the discriminator AC is never actually established
An executor writes `assert len(body) <= 32767` which is also true under Cloud's path (since 32767 == _JIRA_COMMENT_MAX_CHARS) and similarly fails to discriminate
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the AC: 'Concretely: construct a plain-text body of length N where 32000 < N <= 32767 (e.g. N = 32500). Under DC's fit, this fits within WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT and is returned unchanged (or only suffix-marked); under Cloud's ADF mapper, the ADF-serialized form would exceed _ADF_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT (32000) and be truncated further. Assert that pass-1 sends the full 32500-char body (no truncation) and pass-2 plans nothing — if Cloud's mapper were inadvertently used, the ADF inflation would cause pass-1 to truncate the body and pass-2 to detect a delta, turning the test red.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a positive rationale for why `compute_outbound_mutations` (rather than `compute_update_fields` directly) is the right vehicle for the description test — e.g., it mirrors the Cloud test's shape, tests the real public API surface including the three-injector guard, and ensures `links=` propagation is exercised so the OR-fallback cannot silently slip back in.
evidence: Plan text explains what to inject and why all three are needed, but does not state WHY compute_outbound_mutations is the right vehicle rather than compute_update_fields (the inner function that performs description diffing without touching links or comments at all).

outbound_differ.py:384 — compute_outbound_mutations is the public API; compute_update_fields at the inner level would require threading an additional backend stub for just the description diff and would test less of the real pipeline.
Cloud's existing test at test_outbound_description_length_convergence.py:150 drives the same compute_outbound_mutations — this parallel is the natural rationale but the plan does not state it.
findings.finding: The plan does not state a positive rationale for driving the DESCRIPTION convergence test through `compute_outbound_mutations` rather than a more direct inner-layer call (e.g., `compute_update_fields` / `_diff_fields`). Criterion 4 requires the plan state WHY the chosen approach fits — its absence leaves an implementer who questions the choice without an authoritative answer, and without a written rationale the choice can be silently revised to a more direct call that would bypass the three-injector OR-guard the plan specifically warns about.
findings.location: Approach §3, DESCRIPTION convergence paragraph: 'drive compute_outbound_mutations with ALL THREE of outbound_mapper=, inbound_mapper= and links='
scenarios: An implementer who finds compute_outbound_mutations cumbersome (requires binding links=, constructing a transport stub, etc.) might substitute a direct compute_update_fields call, which would bypass the OR-guard the plan specifically warns about — exactly the vacuous-green pattern the plan exists to prevent.
A plan reviewer in a later pass might flag the choice as over-specified without rationale, triggering an unnecessary back-and-forth.
findings.suggested_fix: After 'drive compute_outbound_mutations with ALL THREE of outbound_mapper=, inbound_mapper= and links= bound to a DC backend', add: 'This mirrors the Cloud description test's shape and tests the full public API surface — including the three-injector OR-guard — so a future simplification that drops any one of the three injectors would be caught immediately. Calling `compute_update_fields` directly instead would bypass the guard entirely, reintroducing the config-fallback risk.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Point implementers to the existing `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/backend_support.FakeTransport` (already used by `test_jira_datacenter_backend_port.py`) as the stub transport to use when constructing `JiraDataCenterBackend` for the description convergence test.
evidence: tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/backend_support.py — FakeTransport already implements all 18+ TicketTransport members and is used by JiraDataCenterBackend-based tests (test_jira_datacenter_backend_port.py:59: return JiraDataCenterBackend(transport=FakeTransport()))
A hand-rolled minimal stub risks missing members that JiraDataCenterBackend's constructor or the convergence test path happen to call, producing misleading failures.
The plan says 'stub transport' without naming the existing double — implementers working from this plan alone would not know FakeTransport exists.
findings.finding: The plan instructs the implementer to 'Construct a minimal JiraDataCenterBackend over a stub transport' but does not point to the already-existing `FakeTransport` in `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/backend_support.py`, which is the established DC-test double for this purpose. An implementer who writes a new minimal stub may omit required protocol members (the transport port has 18+ members, per `backend_support.py:63-144`), causing the test to fail for transport-conformance reasons rather than convergence reasons — or, worse, pass despite incorrect setup because a missing member was never called in the convergence path.
findings.location: Approach §3, DESCRIPTION convergence: 'Construct a minimal JiraDataCenterBackend over a stub transport and pass outbound_mapper=b.outbound, inbound_mapper=b.inbound, links=b'
scenarios: Implementer writes a stub with only the members they see referenced in the convergence code path; later a code change touches an additional member and the stub breaks unrelated to convergence.
A stub that returns wrong types from `probe_remote` or `get_comments` could cause test failures unrelated to the DC description-convergence property being tested.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'Construct a minimal JiraDataCenterBackend over a stub transport' with 'Construct a JiraDataCenterBackend using the existing `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/backend_support.FakeTransport` as the transport — this is the established DC-test double (see `test_jira_datacenter_backend_port.py:59`) and already implements all required protocol members.'
